decisions.reason: The rejection is correct: for kappa equal to omega the cardinals kappa_m are finite, so a finite union of kappa_m-element prefix sets need not fit a kappa_m-long list and the defining approximation was unavailable. The repair uses Fleissner's actual finite-set exception, a uniform finite bound depending on the sequence length, and that bound in the Ramsey colouring.

Fact F3 did omit two hypotheses of its construction supplier: kappa must be an infinite cardinal and the cardinal sequence must be increasing. The omission overstated the reusable interface but did not invalidate this application, because kappa is omega and kappa_n=n is increasing. The restatement now includes both hypotheses explicitly.

The former title asserted a formal consistency lower bound, but the proof establishes only an external metatheoretic transformation of any standard finite ZF refutation into one for the NMSC extension. It supplies no proof-code reduction verified in the stated arithmetic base. Renaming the result to a metatheoretic lower bound makes the carrier agree with its statement and proof.

The rejection is correct: Urysohn separation requires the inclusions A subset f^{-1}({0}) and B subset f^{-1}({1}), not equality of the two images with singleton endpoint sets. The equality formulation fails automatically for an empty closed set. This was a false definitional expansion, but the statement and the cited relative-consistency interface already use the correct notion of continuous separation.

The asserted equivalence was false. The even naturals are an infinite subset of the cofinite natural-number space with infinite complement, while the coordinate N inside the cofinite space N union {infinity} has the finite singleton complement {infinity}. Each individual nonclosedness claim is true, so the defect was a non-load-bearing identification; the repair states and verifies them separately.

The rejection identifies a real typing gap: a product point has the coordinate index set as its domain, whereas the cited definition requires a choice function whose domain is the set-family itself. The constructed point still contains the needed values, so the gap is repaired by mapping each family member to the coordinate at its least occurrence and verifying membership and well-definedness.

reviews.reason: Each local family F_theta now has its own at-most-kappa enumeration, whose initial segments exhaust it and whose finite prefix unions are monotone. For kappa greater than omega the usual infinite-cardinal absorption recovers the kappa_n bound; for kappa equal to omega the bound lambda_n is finite and therefore supports finite-colour Ramsey. The nonmetrizability conflict now uses only guarded traces in the actual domain of g, while the normality and ladder-separation cases retain their required hypotheses.

Under CH, kappa=omega is infinite, the sequence kappa_n=n is increasing and cofinal, each 2^n is finite below omega, and 2^omega=omega_1. Nonzero countable limit ordinals form the required stationary set, and the explicit enumeration recursion eventually separates each pair of ladders. These facts meet the repaired construction interface exactly.

The theorem now claims exactly the external consistency implication its finite-proof argument establishes. The proof still identifies the finite fragment used by a hypothetical NMSC refutation, transfers that fragment through the cited interpretation and construction results, and derives a ZF refutation, while explicitly withholding any internal arithmetization or base-verified proof transformer.

Fact F2 now states the endpoint-fibre inclusions that exactly define a Urysohn separator and spells them out pointwise. This handles empty closed sets correctly and makes step 2.1 a faithful expansion of the cited negated Urysohn assertion; no change to the external relative-consistency theorem or its hypotheses is needed.

The revised carrier proves both failures separately. The even set is not closed because its odd complement is nonempty and not cofinite, whereas N is not closed in the enlarged cofinite space because its singleton complement is not open: that singleton has the infinite complement N. The proof now explicitly records why these complement patterns differ.

For each set S in {A_0,A_1,A_2}, the repaired proof takes the least index j with S=A_j and sets g(S)=x_j. This is well-defined even if a finite list repeats a set, and x_j lies in S. The general AC comparison now also distinguishes finite-list reindexing from a product indexed directly by the family.

entries.subject: thm-fleissner-normal-moore-space-construction
entries.evidence: For kappa=omega the original kappa_m-long list could not enumerate the finite union of several kappa_m-sized prefix sets. The repair uses local enumerations and a finite length-dependent bound in the Ramsey case, while infinite-cardinal absorption supplies the original kappa_m bound when kappa>omega.

entries.subject: thm-ch-normal-nonmetrizable-moore-space
entries.evidence: Fact F3 now states that kappa is infinite and that the cardinal sequence is increasing. The CH parameters kappa=omega and kappa_n=n satisfy both conditions, so the repaired supplier interface leaves the application valid.

entries.subject: thm-formal-nmsc-consistency-lower-bound
entries.evidence: The title now calls the result metatheoretic. The item proves an external finite-refutation transformation but no proof-code reduction verified inside the named arithmetic base, so the previous word 'formal' asserted more than the proof supplies.

entries.subject: thm-relative-consistency-countable-choice-without-urysohn
entries.evidence: The negated Urysohn assertion now uses endpoint-fibre inclusions, equivalently pointwise endpoint values. It no longer uses equality of images, which is automatically false when one of the allowed closed sets is empty.

entries.subject: cex-kelley-cofinite-set-is-not-closed
entries.evidence: The carrier now separates the even-naturals counterexample, whose complement is infinite, from the coordinate N in N union {infinity}, whose complement is a singleton. Both nonclosedness claims are proved, without the false assertion that they are equivalent instances.

entries.subject: ex-isolated-point-repair-recovers-choice-function
entries.evidence: The proof now converts the coordinate-indexed product point into a function on the family by choosing each member's least occurrence and proves the selected coordinate belongs to that member. It also distinguishes this finite-list conversion from products indexed directly by the family.
